# E0300: wrong number of type arguments

A generic type takes one type argument per parameter, as `Map<str, i64>` for a map from strings to integers.

- Rule: [`declarations.type-arguments`](../../reference/10-declarations.md#declarations.type-arguments)
- Reported at: the type.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0300:1
fn count(words: Map<str>) -> i64 { words.len() }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn count(words: Map<str, i64>) -> i64 { words.len() }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0300_wrong_number_of_type_arguments.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0300_wrong_number_of_type_arguments.lt):

```text
── WRONG NUMBER OF TYPE ARGUMENTS ── E0300_wrong_number_of_type_arguments.lt:1:17  [E0300]

`Map` takes 2 type arguments, not 1:

  1 │ fn count(words: Map<str>) -> i64 { words.len() }
    │                 ^^^^^^^^

A generic type takes one type argument per parameter, as `Map<str, i64>` for a
map from strings to integers.
```
